correctness.rationale: Joint sampling density sin(a)cos(z)/(8pi) is exact; the spherical cosine formula gives a positive quadratic perimeter deficit z² sin(a)/(2 sin(u)sin(a-u)) on the maximal-perimeter angular sector. The spherical Gram determinant yields a global O(sqrt(epsilon)) transverse bound and proves negligible angular/side endpoint mass. The Dyson gamma integral gives the normalization C*=3pi Gamma(3/4)/Gamma(1/4)^3. Pointwise convergence of rescaled conditional densities plus convergence of mass yields L1/total-variation convergence by Scheffe. The signed transverse mark is uniform on its limiting interval, giving the independent Beta(1/2,1) overshoot. The included checker tests the integral, gamma normalization, and sampling at three thresholds; numerical experiments are corroboration, not proof.
